title: SR-1.28 The bus writes its own routing files
request: Closes G93 (issue #250): connector and device tokens hold write on bus/** (src/engine/devices.mjs:85, src/server/oauth.mjs:17), and the bus's routing files are plain vault notes: bus/operator.json names the operator and bus/seats/<seat>.json carries renamed_from. So a note write makes a cloud connector the operator, its task to the 'operator' alias carries operator authority, and a runner turned on for a local seat starts its command headless with the connector's text as the prompt. Found by the SR-1.25 red-team round and reproduced on 31 October 2026 on the main source. Repository: memev. Depends on contracts: SR-1.27, SR-1.24, QL-1.02. SR-1.27 brings the folded and resolved protected-path check this contract extends to bus/; SR-1.24 brings the admin-gated operator route of issue #248. It is urgent: until it lands, a stopgap fix ahead of it needs the owner's approval. Sensitive path (tokens, the bus and command execution): the QL-1.03 checklist applies before merge.

tasks.title: Bus routing files are written only by the bus
requirements: bus/ joins the internal-only paths: a note-tool write, append or delete under bus/, in any spelling, by SR-1.27's folded and resolved path check, is refused as immutable for every caller, and the bus writes its own files as internal writes

the operator is set only through the admin gate: the admin-gated route of SR-1.24, or bus_set_operator called by a local caller with the admin scope; a bus/operator.json written any other way (by hand, by a sync, by a stale process) is not taken as the operator, and memev doctor reports the drift
renamed_from is written only by the bus's own seat rename, and an entry naming 'operator' or 'all' is refused
a task from a cloud seat never carries operator authority, and a runner starts a command for a task only when its operator authority came from an operator set through the admin-gated route

the trusted lead is kept in .memev/bus-lead.json, written only by the admin-gated route and by bus_set_operator called by a local caller with the admin scope; bus/operator.json is written by the bus for display and sync and is never read as the lead; operator() and the runner read only the trusted lead, on every call
a cloud seat can never be the lead: setting one is refused, and /v1/bus-register never sets a lead

the bus resolves a seat's device and names (renamed_from) from its own records checked against the device registry; a seat file whose device or renamed_from differs from what the bus wrote is ignored for routing and reported by memev doctor

the bus/ guard holds for every token, owner, admin and --remote included, and for the spellings Bus/, bus/Seats/, a backslash, a leading slash and a segment with a trailing dot or space (bus./, 'bus /'), which Windows strips; the refusal code is immutable
a seat rename updates the trusted lead in the same step, and markLeadAsked in src/cli/hooks.mjs goes through the daemon, never writing under bus/ from the hook process

the first start after this change runs a one-time migration: it takes the trusted lead from bus/operator.json only when that names a local seat on this host, and records that the migration ran in config.json, apart from the lead store and in the same step; a vault created after the change records it at creation; once recorded, a missing, empty or corrupt .memev/bus-lead.json means no lead, never a second read of bus/operator.json, and memev doctor says no lead is set and gives the command

a seat is a cloud seat when its device's current kind in the device registry is cloud-connector, and a local seat on this host only when the bus's own record names this host's device id; a seat's name, a machine label and the device_kind field of a seat file play no part

the daemon records each message it sends with operator authority in .memev, binding its id to its recipient and a sha256 of its type and body; a line counts as an operator message only when its id, recipient and hash match that record, and a line that reuses a recorded id with any other recipient or content is ignored and reported

every reader of a message's operator flag (bus.unread, /v1/bus-pulse, renderBus, the stop hook's follow-up in src/cli/hooks.mjs, and holds) uses the verified flag of the requirement above, never the line's own field

SR-1.27's resolved-path check also refuses a note path whose resolved target is under .memev/ or outside the vault root, so a linked folder such as memory/cfg -> ../.memev is refused like memory/b -> ../bus

the runner takes its seat's names from the bus's validated records, as Bus._names does, never from the seat file on disk; an alias that is 'operator', 'all' or another live seat's name is ignored and reported
memev doctor's bus drift checks carry no fix: doctor --fix leaves .memev/bus-lead.json and the seat records as they are, and busChecks reads the trusted lead, never bus/operator.json

memev bus send, memev bus operator and setupBus (init --lead, MEMEV_LEAD, connect, doctor --fix) call the bus with the admin token from .memev/admin.json, so tasks the terminal sends stay operator tasks; a token issued with agent cli and no admin scope gets no operator authority

each red-green criterion of this task that runs test/bus-routing-protected.test.mjs has its own subtest whose name starts with <task>-cNN: (NN is the criterion's position in this task, so T1-c01: for the first), and the criterion runs only that subtest

A task the connector then sends to 'operator' carries operator: false, and a runner turned on for a local seat starts nothing (its run is a recorder).

tasks.title: Bus participation is its own permission
requirements: a newly issued connector or device token gets no bus/** in its paths; bus participation is a separate scope, bus, which the bus routes and the bus MCP tools check
a token issued before this change whose paths include bus/** keeps bus participation and loses nothing else; with T1, its note-tool writes under bus/ are refused like any other caller's
memev token issue and the pairing flows that grant bus access grant the bus scope, and docs/BUS.md says so
clientToken (src/cli/common.mjs) issues connector-URL tokens without bus/** and with the bus scope

a token or OAuth grant issued before this change is marked at migration only when it could use the bus at the base (its paths cover bus/ or are exactly the three pre-bus paths; for OAuth, a grant with the write scope), and keeps bus participation; the mark of an OAuth grant lives on its client record, and refresh copies it to every new access and refresh record; the verify-time path rebuild in src/server/oauth.mjs adds the bus scope to marked grants; a grant with only the read scope keeps reading the bus (bus_unread) and never gains bus_send; the legacy exception in bus.mjs keys on the mark, never on paths
the bus scope grants bus participation only and never widens a token's read or write paths

each red-green criterion of this task that runs test/bus-permission.test.mjs has its own subtest whose name starts with <task>-cNN: (NN is the criterion's position in this task, so T2-c01: for the first), and the criterion runs only that subtest
